findings.rationale: From round 11 onward ME's feature distribution shifts by about 2 federation SDs, mainly on AgeGroup (drift tool). Its uploads change at the same round: update norm jumps to about 3.5x the median and cosine to the median turns negative and keeps worsening. Its local held-out data is off too: CITL +0.108 and ECE 0.099 at round 20, well outside the federation. The pattern fits a feature shift that trains the model away from the others, not clean-data poisoning.

GA's AgeGroup distribution shifts by about 2 federation SDs from round 11 on (drift tool, sustained every round after). Its client-level update statistics are anomalous: lowest mean cosine among large clients, min cosine z=-4.5, and round-20 CITL is elevated (z=+3.7). The feature-level outliers (HighBP, GenHlth, AgeGroup) agree with a shifted population.

MN's features shift by about 2 federation SDs from round 11 on (AgeGroup, GenHlth, HighBP; drift tool). Its uploads are anomalous: median update norm about 2.4x the median, min cosine -0.72 (z=-4.9). Round-20 CITL is high (z=+5.1, ECE z=+3.1), so its local data itself is shifted, which points to drift rather than poisoning.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income) and attribution_churn, then confirmed suspects with per-client drift and update queries. Three clients (ME, GA, MN) show the same signature from round 11 on: AgeGroup/GenHlth feature shift of about 2 SD, anomalous updates (large norm and negative cosine for ME and MN, low cosine for GA), and positive CITL in local performance. I report these as drift with onset round 11. No evidence of poisoning, free-riding, or explanation instability in other clients. Single-statistic outliers in small clients (VI, GU, WY, NC, TN, DE, AK) and a UT AgeGroup-11 O/E outlier were judged to be noise, since they were not confirmed by a second tool. Budget is fully spent (0.0 left).
